FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) was adopted by the Bureau of lndian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Horology Sectional Committee had been approved by the Light Mechanic2 11 Engineering Division Council. In the formulation of this standard, due weightage has been given to the need for international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries. In addition to relating it to the practices being followed in this field in the country. Metric system this system. This standard Part 2 Part 3 has been adopted in India and all dimensions is being published in 3 parts. in this standard have been given in

The other parts are:

Stainless steel straps Link straps relating to leather straps,

This standard is intended chiefly to cover the technical provisions and it does not include all the necessary provisions of a contract.

For the pupose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the .finaI value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

WATCH STRAPS
STRAPS SPECIFICATION

1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 1 ) specifies the dimensions, material, general requirements and methods of test for leather straps for wrist watch. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards adjuncts to this standard:
IS No. Title

5.1.4 Raw Edge Both upper and lining leathers shall be splitted to uniform thickness through the length and cut to the profile of the strap. The cut pieces shall be pasted together with/without reinforceThe edges shall be singed ment in between. and finished see Fig. 2 (b). 5.1.5 Folded on Edge ( Remborded ) Upper and lining leather shall be separately cut split and messed together with adhesive using proper press tool so that raw edge of the lining is not visible see Fig. 2 (c). 5.2 Stitches Stitching pattern shall be as agreed the customer and the manufacturer. 5.3 Loop parts of The dimensions of loop shall be so maintained such that during normal use, the strap shall slide easily through it and shall not come out of the strap either from the buckle end or from the spring bar hole end. The fixed loop shall be fixed at a distance of 6 mm to 12 mm from the buckle end so that the tip of the long end shall enter the fixed loop fully v,hen buckled at the last hole near the tip. The lock stitch of loops is not essential if the g!ued surface with-stand the tensile load test as given in 8.3. 5.4 Spring Bar Hole The spring bar hole shall accommodate spring The thickness of material around bar freely. the spring bar hole shall be uniform. 5.5 Catch Width (W) Catch width Fig. I. shall be maintained as given in between

The bottom surface shall be pasted with lining uniformly split so as to maintain the thickness of the strap. 1 AND FINISH

The buckle design and specification shall be as agreed between I he manufacturer and the customer. The buckles shall be cleaned and deburred by tumbling. The buckles and hooks shall be nickel/gold plated or painted according to the specifications as agreed to between the manufacturer and the customer. 6 MATERIAL 6.1 The material for manufacture of long piece, short piece and loop shall be of leather other than banned or that of endangered species meeting the following requirements:

kg of dry leather. The mildew resistance of leather shall be determined as specified in LB : 2 of IS 6191 : 1971. d) Thread used for stitching shall be cotton cored spun polyester thread. The thread shall withstand a tensile force of 1-Oto 2.0 kgf. 6.2 Skin Compatibility 6.2.1 Watch strap leather shall have the following values: OH

with formaldehyde as its cause may skin irritation. It is also recommended that. leather tanned with chromium do not contain hexavalent chromium, as it may cause allergy. All leathers used in watch strap making must be dyed so that no colour difference through, is seen on cutting surface. The colour of the leather shall not fade when tested for colour fastness at one kg load dry movements 500 strokes, and 150 strokes in wet stage ( result shall be according to grey scale 4 Max ). Leather used in watch strap manufacturing shall not contain pentachlorophenol or any of its derivatives exceeding 5 mg per 3

The tensile strength of the strap shall not be less than 200 N ( 20 kgf) for gents watch straps and 150 N ( 15 kgf ) for ladies watch straps having width below 15 mm at catch. 11.2 The straps shall also be packed in 10 Each pack compartments polythene bags. should contain straps of same catch width colour and pattern. 12 MARKING

9.1 Lot
In a consignment all the straps of the same size and type manufactured from the same material under similar conditions of production shall be grouped together to constitute a lot.

12.1 Leather watch strap shal! be marked/ printed on the backside with the following:
a) Manufacturer's b) Size, and c) Leather mark monogram or genuine or logogramt leather.

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Ruies and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously cheked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS Revision of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indin Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Additions'.
